rules.text: In a sparse switch, an explicit case sharing the default body (`case 100: default:`) still emits its own compare (`cmp r0, #100`) before the branch to that body, while a bare `default:` does not.

A value computed from locals (`int n = (a + b) / 32; h(); k(n);`) can have its computation delayed past an intervening call, while writing the calls inside the expression (`int n = (g() + g()) / 32;`) finishes computing it right after them.
A literal-pool operand shown as `<str:"">` that is loaded and then dereferenced can be a file-local variable: `static T *p;` produces it, while `extern T *p;` shows the symbol name.
`S l = *(const S *)&sym;` (S wraps an array) copies like a local array initializer `int l[6] = {...};`, but the literal pool names `sym` instead of anonymous data.
`if (a() || b() || !c()) return 0;` shares one return block (`bne` to it), while separate `if (a()) return 0;` statements each emit their own return.
Passing an `int` local to a `u8` parameter truncates at the call (`lsls #24; lsrs #24`), while a `u8` local (`u8 x = h();`) is truncated at assignment and passed with a plain move.
An unreferenced `static` function is not emitted; any reference, such as `return (void *)f;` or a non-static `void (*ref)(int *) = f;`, makes the compiler emit it.
`V v = {0, 0, 0};` stores through a base register (`add r0, sp, #N; str r1, [r0, #4]`), while `v.x = 0; v.y = 0; v.z = 0;` stores sp-relative.
In array loops, `T *p = &arr[i]; p->a = src[i];` instead of repeated `arr[i].a = src[i];` can swap the registers holding the strength-reduced pointers.

A large local initializer such as `u16 a[41] = {1, 2};` copies anonymous rodata (`<data:SIZE:HASH>`, so every value must be exact) with a count-down `ldrh`/`strh` loop, unlike a hand-written copy loop from a named table.
`if (x == 3 || x == 4)` folds to a range check (`subs #3; cmp #1; bhi`), while `switch (x) { case 3: case 4: }` emits separate `cmp`/branch pairs.
`d->sub.arr[i] = x;` adds the member offset on every store, while `Sub *s = &d->sub; s->arr[i] = x;` adds the struct offset once and puts the array offset in the `strb` immediate.
If a loop counter and a strength-reduced pointer have swapped callee-saved registers, try separate counters per loop (`i`, `j`) instead of reusing one.
Storing -1 in a loop `a[i] = -1;` emits `subs r0, r1, #1` (from a zero register) for an `s8` array but `movs r0, #255` for a `u8` array.
With an `s16 i`, `i < NELEMS(arr)` compares unsigned (`bcc`), while `i < 60` compares signed (`blt`).
`(g(0) + g(1)) / 2` with `u32` returns divides unsigned (`lsrs #1`), while `(int)(g(0) + g(1)) / 2` emits the signed `lsrs #31; adds; asrs #1`.
`x = x - 7; k(x, ...);` on a `u16` local does the subtract before setting up stack arguments, while `k((u16)(x - 7), ...);` schedules it among them.
`for (i = 0; tbl[i] != 0xFFFF; i++)` over an extern table emits an entry check before the loop, while `do { ... i++; } while (tbl[i] != 0xFFFF);` does not.
A NULL test on a value just copied with `adds rN, rM, #0` needs no `cmp`: `if (p != NULL)` branches on the copy's flags, while `if (p != (int *)4)` emits `cmp rN, #4`.

evidence.a:
#include "types.h"
void k(int *); void f(int a, int *p); void f(int a, int *p) { if (p != NULL) { k(p); k(p); } k((int *)a); }
evidence.b:
#include "types.h"
void k(int *); void f(int a, int *p); void f(int a, int *p) { if (p != (int *)4) { k(p); k(p); } k((int *)a); }

rules.text: `arr[i].a = 0;` in a loop is strength-reduced to a pointer stepped by the element size (`adds r3, #3`), unlike manual byte offsets `*((u8 *)arr + i * 3)`, so write plain indexing.

evidence.a:
#include "types.h"
typedef struct { u8 a, b, c; } S; extern S arr[]; void f(int n); void f(int n) { int i; for (i = 0; i < n; i++) arr[i].a = 0; }
evidence.b:
#include "types.h"
typedef struct { u8 a, b, c; } S; extern S arr[]; void f(int n); void f(int n) { int i; for (i = 0; i < n; i++) *(u8 *)((u8 *)arr + i * 3) = 0; }

rules.text: `A a = f();` for a returned struct builds it in a temporary and then copies it, while `A a; a = f();` can drop the copy when only a member is then read.

evidence.a:
#include "types.h"
typedef struct { u16 x, y, z; } A; A h(void); void k(int); void f(void); void f(void) { A a = h(); k(a.x); }
evidence.b:
#include "types.h"
typedef struct { u16 x, y, z; } A; A h(void); void k(int); void f(void); void f(void) { A a; a = h(); k(a.x); }

rules.text: Assigning an all-zero compound literal `s->v = (V){0, 0, 0};` stores zeros with `str`, while a non-zero one `(V){1, 2, 3}` copies from anonymous rodata (`ldr rN, =<data:...>`).

evidence.a:
#include "types.h"
typedef struct { int x, y, z; } V; typedef struct { int p; V v; } S; void f(S *s); void f(S *s) { s->v = (V){0, 0, 0}; }
evidence.b:
#include "types.h"
typedef struct { int x, y, z; } V; typedef struct { int p; V v; } S; void f(S *s); void f(S *s) { s->v = (V){1, 2, 3}; }

rules.text: A constant aggregate initializer inside a loop body (`for (...) { V s = {4096, 4096, 4096}; g(&s); }`) is loaded into a hidden temporary once before the loop body and copied from it into `s` every iteration, so an early copy can belong to a loop-body local.

evidence.a:
#include "types.h"
typedef struct { int x, y, z; } V; void g(V *); void f(int n); void f(int n) { int i; for (i = 0; i < n; i++) { V s = {4096, 4096, 4096}; g(&s); } }
evidence.b:
#include "types.h"
typedef struct { int x, y, z; } V; void g(V *); void f(int n); void f(int n) { int i; V s = {4096, 4096, 4096}; for (i = 0; i < n; i++) { g(&s); } }

rules.text: Declaration order can set the stack slots of spilled scalar locals: with both spilled, `int a; int b;` put `a` above `b`, and `int b; int a;` swapped them.

evidence.a:
#include "types.h"
int h(int); void k(int, int); void f(int n); void f(int n) { int a; int b; int c; int i; int s = 0; a = h(0); b = h(1); c = h(2); for (i = 0; i < n; i++) { s += h(i); k(s, i); k(s, i); k(s, n); } k(a, b); k(c, 0); }
evidence.b:
#include "types.h"
int h(int); void k(int, int); void f(int n); void f(int n) { int b; int a; int c; int i; int s = 0; a = h(0); b = h(1); c = h(2); for (i = 0; i < n; i++) { s += h(i); k(s, i); k(s, i); k(s, n); } k(a, b); k(c, 0); }

rules.text: A jump-table switch lays out case bodies in source order (writing `case 3:` before `case 0:` moves its body first), so order the C cases by body address after decoding the table.

evidence.a:
#include "types.h"
void k(int); void f(int x); void f(int x) { switch (x) { case 0: k(10); break; case 1: k(21); break; case 2: k(32); break; case 3: k(43); k(44); k(45); break; case 4: k(54); break; } k(0); }
evidence.b:
#include "types.h"
void k(int); void f(int x); void f(int x) { switch (x) { case 3: k(43); k(44); k(45); break; case 0: k(10); break; case 1: k(21); break; case 2: k(32); break; case 4: k(54); break; } k(0); }

rules.text: A small `switch (x)` on 0/1/2 emits all compares first (in ascending value order) and then the bodies in source order, while `if (x == 0) ... else if (x == 1) ...` places each `cmp`/`bne` just before its body.

evidence.a:
#include "types.h"
void k(int); void f(int x); void f(int x) { switch (x) { case 0: k(10); break; case 1: k(21); break; case 2: k(32); break; } k(0); }
evidence.b:
#include "types.h"
void k(int); void f(int x); void f(int x) { if (x == 0) { k(10); } else if (x == 1) { k(21); } else if (x == 2) { k(32); } k(0); }

rules.text: Comparison constants are kept as written: `x < 8` emits `cmp #8; bge`, while `x <= 7` emits `cmp #7; bgt`.

evidence.a:
#include "types.h"
void k(int); void f(int x); void f(int x) { if (x < 8) k(1); k(0); }
evidence.b:
#include "types.h"
void k(int); void f(int x); void f(int x) { if (x <= 7) k(1); k(0); }

rules.text: Assigning an int expression to a narrow local truncates at the assignment (`u16 v = x + 3;` adds `lsls #16; lsrs #16`, `u8` uses #24, even if the value already fits), while `int v` does not.

evidence.a:
#include "types.h"
void k(int); void f(int x); void f(int x) { u16 v = x + 3; k(v); k(v); }
evidence.b:
#include "types.h"
void k(int); void f(int x); void f(int x) { int v = x + 3; k(v); k(v); }

rules.text: Parentheses control constant arithmetic order: `a + b - 5` adds then subtracts, while `a + (b - 5)` subtracts from `b` first.

evidence.a:
#include "types.h"
int f(int a, int b); int f(int a, int b) { return a + b - 5; }
evidence.b:
#include "types.h"
int f(int a, int b); int f(int a, int b) { return a + (b - 5); }

rules.text: Operand order of a multiply can set load order: `s->a * s->b` loads `a` first and `s->b * s->a` loads `b` first.

evidence.a:
#include "types.h"
typedef struct { int a, b; } S; int f(S *s); int f(S *s) { return s->a * s->b; }
evidence.b:
#include "types.h"
typedef struct { int a, b; } S; int f(S *s); int f(S *s) { return s->b * s->a; }

rules.text: Address-taken locals of one block (scalars, arrays, structs) are placed by declaration order, the earlier declared at the higher stack address: `T t; int ids[6];` puts `ids` below `t`.

evidence.a:
#include "types.h"
typedef struct { int a[5]; } T; void g(void *, void *); void f(void); void f(void) { T t; int ids[6]; g(&t, ids); }
evidence.b:
#include "types.h"
typedef struct { int a[5]; } T; void g(void *, void *); void f(void); void f(void) { int ids[6]; T t; g(&t, ids); }

rules.text: Local declaration order affects which register each local gets (and can decide which one is spilled): `int i; int *r = NULL;` versus `int *r = NULL; int i;` swaps r4/r5.

evidence.a:
#include "types.h"
int *h(int); int c(int *); int *f(void); int *f(void) { int i; int *r = NULL; for (i = 0; i < 6; i++) { if (c(h(i))) r = h(i); } return r; }
evidence.b:
#include "types.h"
int *h(int); int c(int *); int *f(void); int *f(void) { int *r = NULL; int i; for (i = 0; i < 6; i++) { if (c(h(i))) r = h(i); } return r; }
